answer: Reusing one run across aliases collides on the summit identifier and voids the later submissions, thus the operator pays for 238 runs and collects one. Because the shale index holds every id for the epoch, the collision is provable from the ledger, and the pulse audit republishes the full set. Each answer commits to a run identifier that must be unique within the epoch, so 238 answers need 238 separate inference runs with separate seeds.
